newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis repeats France wants stable franc.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis repeats France wants stable franc.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis reiterated on Friday that the government strongly supported a stable franc in Europe, adding this was a condition for low interest rates needed for growth and employment.

"(Arthuis) reaffirms that the government is very firmly attached to the stability of the franc at the heart of the European Monetary System," the finance ministry said in a statement issued on Friday evening.
"This stability guarantees that the purchasing power of French people is maintained," the statement said.
"It is the condition for obtaining the lowest possible interest rates. These are what create the conditions for growth and employment," it said.
The statement was issued shortly after Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet issued his own statement designed to squash talk of a possible depreciation in the franc.

Trichet said nothing would justify a depreciation of the franc against the most credible currencies in the Exchange Rate Mechanism of the EMS, and the Bank of France was unshakeably committed to the franc's stability against those currencies.
